summary: Gates County, NC: a 120-foot four-legged tower of 1942 on state land at a Forest Service site; a 2018 surplus auction is the last recorded event.

facts.design: Four-legged standard Forest Service lookout tower
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: 120-foot tower, credited to private sources in the 1942 state report quoted on the Forest Lookouts page
North Carolina Geodetic Survey described the station: 120-foot four-legged Forest Service tower, station at its center
Survey station recovered by US Power Squadron, in good condition
Auction of surplus state property opened for bids on March 22, 2018; the tower is said to be on state land at a Forest Service headquarters site; the outcome is not in the sources

notes_for_editor: Only two sources describe this tower: the Forest Lookouts page and the NGS datasheet (the 1980 station description and the 1997 recovery). The 2018 auction is the latest event in them and its outcome is not stated. The 1980 NGS location (U.S. 158 Bypass at Eleanors Crossroads) is not said to be the same place as the 2018 Forest Service headquarters site, so the story does not join them. The 1942 construction credit (private sources) and the state agency are both as the Forest Lookouts page gives them; the page does not explain the difference. The ncstatesurplus.com notice the page cites was not fetched, and it may show the auction result. No photo found. Status and access are unknown.
